carnival-horizon.title: Carnival Horizon: Specs, Class, CDC Score
carnival-horizon.description: Carnival lists Horizon at 133,500 gross tons and 3,960 guests, in service since 2018. Fincantieri calls it Vista class and also prints 133,596. CDC score 95 on 8 Feb 2026.
carnival-horizon.lead: Carnival Horizon is a Vista-class ship. Fincantieri, the builder, calls it a sister to Carnival Vista and lists delivery in 2018. Carnival's ship page and fact sheet both list 133,500 gross tons, a guest capacity of 3,960, and 1,450 crew.
paragraphs: Fincantieri's product page says 133,500 tons in the introduction and prints 133,596 in the specification table on the same page. Carnival's public figure is 133,500. Use Carnival's number for the line's capacity claims, and treat 133,596 as the builder's table figure.
Carnival.com lists length as 1,055 feet. Fincantieri lists length overall as 323.4 meters. This page does not convert one into the other.
Fincantieri lists 1,987 passenger cabins and a maximum of 6,538 persons on board. That persons figure is larger than Carnival's guest capacity of 3,960. Do not read 6,538 as double occupancy.
This page uses those published pages and the CDC green sheet. It does not describe a sailing we took.

sections.heading: Entertainment
paragraphs: The same page names the theater, water park, and adult areas below. It also says the ship has three age-specific youth spaces.

sections.heading: Cabins
paragraphs: Carnival sorts staterooms into interior, ocean view, balcony, and suite headings, then repeats many of them as Havana, Cloud 9 Spa, or Family Harbor versions. Havana headings say guests must be 12 or older. Family Harbor headings list a lounge, kids-eat-free at most specialty restaurants, and one evening of Night Owls babysitting. Cloud 9 headings list thermal-suite access and priority spa bookings. The page does not print square footage in those headings.

Fincantieri's cabin table, which is a count rather than a name list, shows 729 standard inside cabins, 883 balcony cabins, 64 window cabins, 215 window deluxe and family cabins, 49 suites, 8 penthouse suites, and 25 fully accessible cabins.

carnival-sunrise.description: Carnival's fact sheet lists Sunrise at 101,509 gross tons and 2,984 guests, entered service 1999. A 2018 Carnival release said Triumph would be renamed Sunrise. CDC score 100 on 12 Feb 2026.
carnival-sunrise.lead: Carnival Sunrise is the ship Carnival renamed from Carnival Triumph. A 31 Jul 2018 Carnival announcement said a Cadiz dry dock would lead to the new name and place the ship in the Sunshine class. Carnival's fact sheet now lists entered service as 1999, 101,509 gross tons, and double occupancy of 2,984.
paragraphs: An earlier version of this page listed 2014. That year is wrong against Carnival's fact sheet, which lists 1999. This database still files the ship as Destiny class. Carnival's 2018 announcement said the renamed ship would join the Sunshine class. Those are two labels for one hull.

The fact sheet's shipyard field reads Cadiz, Spain. The 2018 announcement describes Cadiz as the dry-dock yard for the rename, starting 1 Mar 2019. Do not read that field as a claim about the original builder. Carnival's fact sheet does not name the original yard.
The ship page matches the fact sheet on tonnage, the 2,984 guest capacity, 1,108 crew, and a length of 893 feet.

wonder-of-the-seas.title: Wonder of the Seas: Specs and CDC Score
wonder-of-the-seas.description: Royal Caribbean's 11 Sep 2025 guide lists Wonder at 235,600 gross tons, 18 decks, and 5,734 guests at double occupancy. CDC score 99 on 13 Feb 2026. The guide's 'largest ship' line is stale.

paragraphs: That same guide still calls Wonder the largest cruise ship in the world. Treat that superlative as stale. Icon of the Seas is already in service in this database, and the guide's own date is 11 Sep 2025. This page uses the measurements and does not repeat 'largest' as a current fact.
The guide does not print a maximum berth count above the 5,734 double-occupancy figure. This page does not repeat an older unsourced maximum.

disney-dream.lead: Disney Dream is grouped on this site with Disney Fantasy in the Dream class. Disney's technical information sheet lists 129,690 gross tons, a length of 339.8 meters (1,114.7 feet), builder Meyer Werft in Papenburg, keel laid August 2009, and delivery in December 2010.
paragraphs: That sheet does not print a guest count. This page does not repeat an older maximum, because that number is not on the sheet. This database still carries 2011 as the in-service year. The sheet lists delivery in December 2010 and does not print a maiden-voyage date.
The sheet was retrieved from Disney Cruise Line Blog, which hosts the Disney document. Figures below are the ones printed on that sheet.
This page uses that sheet, Disney's ship and dining pages, and the CDC green sheet. It does not describe a sailing we took.

Disney's Royal Palace page says Royal Palace is a main dining room in rotational dining on all Disney ships. Disney's Enchanted Garden page uses that same all-ships line. Confirm the rotational set on your sailing, because an all-ships sentence can lag a new ship.
Those pages do not print prices.

msc-poesia.title: MSC Poesia: Specs, Class, CDC Score
msc-poesia.description: MSC's technical sheet lists Poesia at 92,627 gross tons and 13 guest decks. Passenger counts disagree across MSC pages. A 15 Apr 2026 release added the Yacht Club. CDC score 97 on 23 Apr 2026.
msc-poesia.lead: MSC Poesia is a Musica-class ship. MSC's 15 Apr 2026 release says she is the second of the four Musica-class ships through a Palumbo Malta dry dock, after MSC Magnifica. The same release says the work added the MSC Yacht Club before Alaska sailings from Seattle.
paragraphs: MSC's technical sheet lists 92,627 gross tons, 16 decks including 13 for guests, length 293.80 meters, beam 32.20 meters, height 59.64 meters, and a maximum speed of 23 knots. It lists 3,223 passengers, 1,275 cabins, and about 987 crew.

MSC's public ship pages do not agree with each other, or with that sheet, on the head count. The Canada page lists 3,013 passengers, about 987 crew, and 1,229 cabins. The Australia page lists 3,223 passengers, about 1,039 crew, and 1,223 cabins. An earlier version of this page listed 2,550 guests at double occupancy. That figure is not on these current MSC pages. Do not use 2,550.
Suite counts also disagree. The 15 Apr 2026 release says 69 Yacht Club suites. The Canada and Australia pages say 63 suites, available from 23 Apr 2026. Confirm the count in the booking flow.
This database still lists 2008 as the in-service year. The technical sheet and the April 2026 release do not restate a delivery year, so this page does not treat 2008 as a freshly checked fact.
This page uses MSC's documents and the CDC green sheet. It does not describe a sailing we took.
